Order 
1. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the claimant arising out of the award dated 23.03.2013 passed by IInd Additional Member, M.A.C.T., Gwalior in Claim Case No.23/2012 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation as well as aggrieved by the finding of Claims Tribunal that Insurance Company was totally exonerated from its liability.
2. The date of accident and negligence are not in dispute and the findings of the Tribunal in this regard is not in question.

3. As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of injury received by Gopal Singh, Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.16,335/- with interest from the date of filing of claim application till its realization.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the claimant submitted that Claims Tribunal has committed error in awarding the compensation amount.
The Claims Tribunal awarded compensation is on the lower side.
It is further submitted that claimant has received so many injuries in the alleged accident.
He has also submitted that claimant has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- in his treatment.
The Claims Tribunal has also committed error in exonerating the insurance company from its liability.
Counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that offending vehicle weighs below than 7500 k.g., so there is no need of endorsement to drive the vehicle.
Hence, prayed for enhancement of compensation by setting aside the order of the Claims Tribunal.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prays for dismissal of this appeal.
6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, it is undisputed that the alleged accident was occurred by an Auto rickshaw bearing Registration No.MP07-R- 4333.
It is also undisputed that weight of the vehicle was less than 7500 Kg and at the time accident, Driver of the offending vehicle has carried driving licence of LMV.

In the case of Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. AIR 2017 SC 3668, the Apex Court held that:-
"(ii) A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg. would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, 'unladen weight' of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in section 10(2)(d)
is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg. or a motor car or tractor or road-roller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

sentences.text:
That is to say, no separate endorsement on the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:17201 3 MA-678-2013 licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.

A licence issued under section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54/1994 and 28.3.2001 in the form"
7.

In view of the aforesaid verdict, it is clear that no separate endorsement on license is required to drive transport vehicle, so finding of the Claims Tribunal in this regard is erroneous and is hereby set aside.
8.
Now, heard on the question of enhancement of compensation.

9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and more particularly the age of injured and injuries received by him, it shall be appropriate to enhance the amount by Rs.25,000/- in addition to the amount already awarded by Claims Tribunal, which shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the Claims Tribunal in its award from the date of filing of the application.
10. Resultantly, this appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above.

The insurance company is liable to pay the enhanced amount o f Rs.25,000/- to the Gopal Singh Kushwah vs Ballu @ Rajendra Singh Tathore on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157999294/
